title: Paranormal investigation group to host first event of its kind in the Highlands
excerpt: According to the team leader, the chosen location for the event has a deep paranormal history.
content:
A group which investigates paranormal activity in the Highlands is hosting a special convention - the first of its kind in the region.

Highland Paranormal, formed in 2010, is hosting ‘Paracon’, with panels, workshops and a whole host of eerie activities on offer.

Starting 6pm on November 20 in Strathpeffer, it will continue through the daytime on November 21 (Saturday).

Attendees can look forward to talks from the likes of folklorist Kate Ray, artist Linda Mackay, who honours the women persecuted under the witchcraft act, and UFO researcher Malcolm Robinson.

Team leader Liam Shand says that Strathpeffer suits the event to the last detail.

He said: “It's an opportunity to celebrate Haunted Highlands! We live in such a wonderful part of the world with so much folklore, ghost stories and history. It's great to be able to share that with others.

“We'll be talking especially about the Strathpeffer area and the ghost stories around Strathpeffer, its links with the Brahan Seer, and even Aleister Crowley who visited there. His wife to be stayed in the village and that's where they met.

“There are lots of different links. If you go further back, there's even the story that the devil himself bathes in the spa pools above Strathpeffer.

“We've investigated both our venue - the Highland Hotel - and the Pavilion. We've had reports of activity in both buildings. There's lots going on for such a small village, and such a new village, because Strathpeffer actually only came into existence in the late 1800s.”

Liam also corroborated words from those who attended Highland Realms Comic Con - not having to travel large distances for an event like this feels like a huge breakthrough.

He said: “Another reason to do it is to give the Highlands something a bit different. It's not the standard run-of-the-mill market.

“I was in Edinburgh for Comic Con Scotland and it's a trek. It's a hotel and travel. The fact I can be back within half an hour is a huge plus.

“We've got the residential tickets that people were able to buy to stay in the hotel, but we've got day tickets as well. People who live locally and don't want to stay in the hotel can now get their ticket, come along for Saturday and enjoy the day.”

Highland Paracon’s roster is filled with faces from far and wide, so Liam encouraged people not to miss out.

He said: “It's a great opportunity to come and listen to some great experts in the field. If you're interested in the paranormal, it’s most certainly not to be missed.

“These are folks who don't normally come this far north to do conventions, so we're very lucky to have them.

The Highland Paranormal team is already thinking forward, with interest from overseas already brewing.

“We have been approached about doing one next year, but we'll wait and see. We'd be moving forward and then trying to do it even bigger and better, and have tie-ins with America as well.

“We've got a tour company in America who are really keen to get involved. They do paranormal tours across the world.”
